_meta.indication: Indicated in adult patients with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis (inducing/maintaining clinical response and remission, improving endoscopic appearance of the mucosa, corticosteroid-free remission) and with moderately to severely active Crohn's disease (achieving clinical response, clinical remission, and corticosteroid-free remission) who had an inadequate response with, lost response to, or were intolerant to a TNF blocker or immunomodulator, or corticosteroids.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study C13006 (UC induction and maintenance; corresponds to label UC Trials I and II)
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with separate induction and maintenance phases
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis defined as Mayo score of six to 12 with endoscopy subscore of two or three
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Induction: clinical response at Week 6. Maintenance: clinical remission at Week 52.
pivotal_trials.n: UC Trial I: 374 randomized; UC Trial II: 373 randomized
pivotal_trials.result: UC Trial I clinical response at Week 6: 47% ENTYVIO vs 26% placebo (p<0.001; difference 22%). UC Trial II clinical remission at Week 52: 42% (every 8 weeks) vs 16% placebo (p<0.001; difference 26%).

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study C13007 (CD induction and maintenance; corresponds to label CD Trials I and III)
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in moderately to severely active Crohn's disease (CDAI 220 to 450) with separate induction and maintenance phases
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with moderately to severely active Crohn's disease (CDAI score of 220 to 450)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Induction: clinical remission (CDAI <=150) at Week 6. Maintenance: clinical remission at Week 52.
pivotal_trials.n: CD Trial I (induction): 368 randomized; CD Trial III (maintenance): 461 randomized
pivotal_trials.result: CD Trial I clinical remission at Week 6: 15% ENTYVIO vs 7% placebo (p=0.04; difference 8%). CD Trial III clinical remission at Week 52: 39% (every 8 weeks) vs 22% placebo (p=0.001; difference 17%).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=3% and >=1% higher than placebo) included nasopharyngitis (13% vs 7%), headache (12% vs 11%), arthralgia (12% vs 10%), nausea (9% vs 8%) and pyrexia (9% vs 7%). Serious adverse reactions occurred in 7% of ENTYVIO patients vs 4% placebo. Warnings include infusion/hypersensitivity reactions, infections, PML, and liver injury.
target_moa: Vedolizumab is a humanized monoclonal antibody that specifically binds the alpha4beta7 integrin and blocks its interaction with MAdCAM-1, inhibiting migration of memory T-lymphocytes into inflamed gastrointestinal tissue; it does not bind the alpha4beta1 or alphaEbeta7 integrins (gut-selective).

advisory_committee.vote: Joint Advisory Committee meeting held December 9, 2013. CD induction efficacy vote YES=12; NO=9; ABSTAIN=0. CD maintenance efficacy vote YES=19; NO=1; ABSTAIN=1. CD benefit-risk vote A=14; B=6; C=1. The majority voted to approve for both CD induction and maintenance.

summary.text: Standard BLA (351(a)) received June 20, 2013 and approved on this cycle; the regulatory review focused on PML risk and Crohn's efficacy, which were discussed at a joint Advisory Committee on December 9, 2013. The approval carried required pediatric and 505(o) safety studies.

citations.quote: Please refer to your Biologics License Application (BLA) dated and received June 20, 2013, submitted under section 351(a) of the Public Health Service Act for Entyvio (vedolizumab).

My review will focus on key review issues that were presented and discussed at an Advisory Committee meeting (Joint Meeting of the Gastrointestinal Drugs Advisory Committee and the Drug Safety and Risk Management Advisory Committee) on December 9, 2013.

requirement.text: Under 505(o): a postmarketing, prospective, observational cohort study of vedolizumab versus other agents for IBD with primary outcome of serious infections and secondary outcomes including PML, malignancy, and specific infections.

citations.quote: - A postmarketing, prospective, observational, cohort study of vedolizumab versus other agents for inflammatory bowel disease. The study's primary outcome is serious infections. Secondary outcomes include, but are not limited to, progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML), malignancy, and specific infections including gastrointestinal and upper respiratory infections.

requirement.text: Complete Clinical Trial C13008, an open-label trial to determine the long-term safety of Entyvio in patients with ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease, including serious infections (PML) and malignancies.
